newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia government calls truckers' strike illegal.
newsitem.headline: Colombia government calls truckers' strike illegal.

text.p: The Colombian government declared a strike by truck drivers illegal on Friday in a bid to end the five-day-old work stoppage that has shut down the country's export industries and dealt a serious blow to the economy.
The move was announced by Labour Minister Orlando Obregon, who said the strike had been outlawed by the government with immediate effect.
"We have declared the suspension of activities by transporters illegal," Obregon said in an interview with the Caracol radio network.

It was not immediately clear how the government would enforce the measure, however, since the tens of thousands of truck drivers were participating in the strike work independently of the government and have no formal obligation to provide services to anyone.

Olga Rosero Legarba, a leader of the independent Colombian Truckers Association, said the strike would continue "indefinitely," despite the government move. She said the only way authorities could succeed in ending it was by intervening with shipping agencies and transportation companies to force them to provide a better standard of living for truckers.
